verdict: The headline finding — warm starts select among materially different converged solutions, and HJB residual accuracy cannot arbitrate — is important and the randomized design is sound. But as a note about a ROBUST control problem it reports only the maximizing player's half of the solution. At xi=0.05 the solution IS the pair (policies, worst-case model): the drift distortions h = -(1/xi)sigma'V_x and jump-belief distortions g = exp(-(V^l - V)/xi) are part of the delivered object, and the note's own numbers (marginal values 1.6-1.8x higher, welfare level "about 0.6" higher) imply the two economies carry different worst-case beliefs — with the jump beliefs amplified by 1/xi = 20, so the vague "about 0.6 in every jump state" hides exactly the quantity that decides whether the two solutions share a worst-case model. The single-xi comparison also cannot distinguish plain PDE weak identification from robustness-induced selection, even though the networks take log-xi as a pseudo-state and the full xi-profile of the gap is available at zero training cost. Finally, the deliberate agnosticism about which solution is "correct" is currently evasive rather than tenable: for fixed xi this HJB system should have a unique (viscosity) solution, and unused arbitration tools exist in-house — a finite-difference solution of the 3-state terminal regime, a symmetric cross-path residual matrix, box-wide sup residuals, and cross-plugging each pre-jump V against the other family's post-jump V. Agnosticism is legitimate only after those tests fail to separate the candidates. Conditionally acceptable after the demands below; the deep-xi wave must be pre-registered with validity criteria or it will measure the team's known xi*~0.025 level-identification wall rather than warm-start selection.
major_points: No worst-case distortions are reported. Under multiplier preferences the minimizing player's choice (h_d, h_g, h_r, h_y and g^l, g^l', g^l'') is part of the equilibrium, not a diagnostic. Two economies with marginal values differing by 1.6-1.8x mechanically imply Brownian distortions h differing by the same factors, and nber's ~4x dirty capital raises emissions E, which enters both h_y = -(1/xi) V_y E varsigma and the damage-jump intensity region. The note must report the distorted (worst-case) objects — distortion histograms and worst-case temperature/damage-jump densities — for reference vs nber. (This is also the team's own mandatory PI-report set.)

The statement that nber's welfare level sits 'about 0.6 higher in every jump state' is fatally imprecise at xi=0.05. Jump beliefs depend on CROSS-REGIME differences V^l - V multiplied by 1/xi = 20: if the +0.6 shift is uniform across regimes it cancels in g; if it is uniform only to within ~0.03, worst-case jump probabilities differ by factors of order e^0.6. Report V^l - V per jump channel along the path to 1e-3 precision, and the implied g's.

Comparing at a single xi is inadequate and unnecessary: log-xi is a pseudo-state input, so the trained networks already contain the whole xi-family. Whether the nber-reference gap is flat in xi (plain HJB weak identification) or grows like 1/xi (robustness-channel selection, consistent with the confirmed delta-anchor level-identification defect where residual slack in the LEVEL is amplified by exp(-(V^l - V)/xi)) is THE mechanism question, and the note does not ask it.

Comparing at matched xi is not comparing at matched robustness. The interpretable budget in the Hansen-Sargent tradition is the relative entropy / detection-error probability of the worst-case model, and two solutions at the same xi can sit at very different entropy. Without the entropy accounting, 'both solved at xi=0.05' does not mean the two planners fear comparably distorted models.

The agnostic stance ('we do not claim either is correct') is not yet earned. Available arbitration: (a) the terminal post-damage post-tech regime is 3-state, jump-free, and has an in-house FD solution — if reference and nber disagree there, one is simply wrong at the boundary of the backward induction and the 'coherent alternative' framing collapses; (b) the 10x-lower-error claim is asymmetric — it is one solution's residual on one path; a 2x2 cross-path matrix plus box-wide statistics is required before writing 'accuracy does not arbitrate'; (c) the known level-slack direction (residual sensitivity to a pure level shift is only -delta = -0.01) means path-RMS residual systematically under-penalizes level errors — the very dimension on which the solutions differ by 0.6.

The mid-study clamp of jump-belief exponents to [-60, 60] modifies the minimizing player's problem (it truncates the entropy penalty's reach). The note must state whether the reference run's production code carried the same clamp, and report clamp-activation frequency for every converged arm at every evaluated xi. At xi=0.005 the exponent is 200(V^l - V), so this is not hypothetical: a binding clamp means the deep-xi arms solve a different robust control problem.

The deep-xi wave (floor 0.005) lacks a measurement protocol. Without pre-registered validity criteria it will conflate warm-start selection with the known xi*~0.025 level-identification wall; specify in advance what is measured (gap vs xi, distortions, entropy, clamp activation, seed spread) and what disqualifies the xi=0.005 point.
minor_points: Loss_v comparability: within the 1M wave the shared sampling distribution justifies comparison, but the deep-xi wave changes the log-xi sampling range, so its loss_v is NOT comparable to this wave's — flag this before appending results to the same report.

The analytic arm's failure (right level, wrong shape, overflow of exp(-(V^l - V)/xi) at initialization) is itself direct evidence for the 1/xi level-amplification mechanism behind the selection story; connect it explicitly instead of leaving it as an incident-log curiosity.

The perturb arms' 12% seed spread in policies may imply much larger spread in worst-case jump beliefs (x20 amplification); include perturb in the distortion comparison rather than only in the policy fan.

R&D is described as 'nearly doubled' for nber but no i_r or knowledge-stock numbers appear in any table; add I_r (or RD) at year 60 alongside I_g/I_d, minding the team's own level-vs-ratio dictionary.

'Randomized comparison'/RCT with n=2 seeds per arm: within-method spread estimates rest on two draws; say so, and consider a third seed for the two arms (nber, perturb) whose spread carries inferential weight.

Post-damage regimes should be evaluated at the damage-threshold entry slice Y = y-hat only (the note's figure caption suggests this is done — state it as a rule, since 'in the training box' is not 'economically visited').

demanded_experiments.name: Worst-case distortion comparison at xi=0.05
demanded_experiments.design: For reference, nber_s1/s2, and perturb_s1/s2 (frozen networks, no retraining): simulate 10,000 paths over 60 years under each solution's own policies; at each point compute h_d, h_g, h_r, h_y (closed forms, Sec. 7.1, with the regime-correct (logN)_y in h_y) and g^l (l=1..5), g^l', g^l''. Report overlaid histograms at t = 20/40/60, the implied cumulative worst-case damage-jump and tech-jump probabilities over 60 years, and the worst-case temperature density. Also tabulate the cross-regime gaps V^l - V along the path to 1e-3.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether the two converged economies imply materially different worst-case beliefs: the comparison statistic is the difference in worst-case 60-year damage-jump probability (and in median g per channel) between nber and reference, judged against the within-method seed spread. If distinguishable, the note's economic-comparison section is incomplete without them; if the g's coincide because the +0.6 level shift is uniform across regimes, that is itself a sharp finding (pure level multiplicity, beliefs shared).

demanded_experiments.name: xi-profile of the selection gap (zero training cost)
demanded_experiments.design: Evaluate the already-trained 1M networks on a log-xi grid spanning the sampled range, e.g. xi in {148, 1, 0.3, 0.1, 0.05} (extend with {0.025, 0.01, 0.005} once the deep wave lands); simulate paths at each xi; report gap(xi) = (I_g^nber - I_g^ref)/I_g^ref at year 60, plus Delta(V), Delta(V_logK), Delta(V_logR) along paths, with the two nber seeds plotted separately. Hold everything else fixed; only the evaluation xi varies.
demanded_experiments.decides: The mechanism. Gap approximately flat in xi ⇒ plain HJB weak identification unrelated to robustness; gap growing as xi falls (roughly like 1/xi in the belief-sensitive quantities) ⇒ selection operates through the robustness channel, i.e. the level-identification defect amplified by the jump distortion. Also determines whether 'comparison at a single xi' understates or overstates the selection effect.

demanded_experiments.name: Terminal-regime FD arbitration
demanded_experiments.design: Solve the post-damage post-tech regime (3 states: logK, Z, Y; no jump terms) by the in-house finite-difference/ADI solver at xi=0.05 and xi=infinity on the training box. Compare reference and nber value LEVEL, V_logK, V_Z against FD: RMS and sup over the box and along the entry slice Y = y-hat. Estimate FD discretization error by grid refinement so the tolerance band is principled.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether the multiplicity originates at the boundary of the backward induction. If one candidate deviates from FD by more than the FD refinement error while the other matches, the agnostic stance is untenable: the deviating solution is inaccurate at the terminal node and the error propagates forward through the jump-expectation terms. If both match FD at the terminal node, agnosticism gains real support and the multiplicity must arise in the jump-coupled regimes.

demanded_experiments.name: Symmetric residual matrix + cross-plugging
demanded_experiments.design: Compute true per-regime HJB residuals (rhs - pv form, not the training loss) for each of {reference, nber} evaluated along BOTH simulated paths (2x2 matrix) and on a fixed LHS sample over the whole box (RMS and 99th percentile), at xi=0.05. Additionally cross-plug: recompute the pre-damage pre-tech residual using nber's own V but the reference's downstream (post-jump) value functions inside the jump terms, and vice versa.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether 'accuracy does not arbitrate' survives symmetric evaluation (the current 10x claim is one cell of the matrix). The cross-plug decides the structure of the difference: if swapping downstream V's inflates the residual by approximately the jump-term response to the ~0.6 level offset, the two candidates are internally consistent families differing chiefly by a common level — pointing back at the delta-anchor defect rather than genuine PDE multiplicity.

demanded_experiments.name: Relative-entropy and detection-error accounting
demanded_experiments.design: For each converged solution at xi=0.05: along the simulated paths compute the discounted relative entropy of the worst-case model, split into the Brownian part (1/2)|h|^2 and the jump part sum_l J^l (1 - g^l + g^l log g^l); and a 60-year detection-error probability by simulating the log-likelihood ratio between the worst-case and baseline models under both measures.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether matched xi is matched robustness. If nber's worst-case entropy exceeds the reference's by more than ~2x, the two planners are not comparably robust and the note should re-do the headline comparison at matched entropy (the constraint-preference dual) or at matched detection-error probability, not matched xi.

demanded_experiments.name: Pre-registered deep-xi wave protocol (floor 0.005)
demanded_experiments.design: Before results land, fix the measurement set: (a) gap(xi) from the xi-profile experiment extended to {0.025, 0.01, 0.005}; (b) g-distortions and entropy at xi = 0.005; (c) clamp-activation rate — fraction of training-batch points and of simulated-path points where the jump exponent |(V^l - V)/xi| >= 60 — per regime per xi, for every arm AND stated for the reference's production code; (d) within-method seed spread at each xi. Disqualification rule fixed in advance: a xi point is reported as uninterpretable if the clamp binds on more than 1% of path points, or if same-arm seeds disagree by more than half the between-arm (nber vs reference) gap at that xi.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether warm-start selection at deep xi is measurable at all before the known xi*~0.025 level-identification wall and clamp saturation contaminate it. If the gap grows into the wall region only where the disqualification rule triggers, the correct conclusion is 'deep-xi selection is confounded with the level defect', not 'selection grows with aversion'.

initialization_proposals.name: xi-homotopy from the uncertainty-neutral limit
initialization_proposals.construction: Train the four regimes cold at xi = infinity (in practice logxi at the top of the sampled range, where the jump bracket is linear sum_l J^l (V^l - V) and the -1/(2xi) drag vanishes), then continue training down a xi ladder (e.g. 148 -> 1 -> 0.3 -> 0.1 -> 0.05 -> 0.025), each rung warm-started from the previous rung's weights, same schedule and budget split. This is the M6 curriculum arm listed in STUDY.md but apparently never run — run it.
initialization_proposals.rationale: At xi = infinity the exp amplification is absent and the HJB is far better conditioned, so cold training has its best chance of converging to the (presumably unique) neutral solution; the homotopy then isolates whether multiplicity is robustness-induced: if the rung solutions track a single branch down to xi=0.05, the branch it lands on (reference-like or nber-like) is the continuation of the neutral solution — the most decision-theoretically defensible selection criterion on offer, and it produces the gap(xi) curve as a by-product.

initialization_proposals.name: FD-anchored terminal init with FOC-consistent controls
initialization_proposals.construction: Replace the failed anchor arm's regression target (the arm's own trained post-post net) with the finite-difference post-damage post-tech solution: Sobolev-fit each regime's value net to the FD V AND its first derivatives (V_logK, V_Z, V_y) on the box; initialize controls not cold but from the closed-form FOCs evaluated at the fitted derivatives (phi'-inversion for i_d, i_g; psi_r'-inversion for i_r). Pre-tech regimes fit to the FD terminal V as a common shape prior.
initialization_proposals.rationale: The anchor arm failed with cold controls and a self-referential target; this variant pins the backward induction's boundary to a non-neural ground truth and starts the maximizing player at FOC-consistency, removing the two failure modes observed. It also doubles as an arbitration arm: if it converges to nber rather than the reference (or vice versa), that identifies which family is the continuation of the FD-correct terminal node.

initialization_proposals.name: Belief-neutral (g = 1) common-value init
initialization_proposals.construction: Initialize ALL regimes' value networks to the SAME function (fit each to one common target, e.g. the analytic level v ~ logK + const or the FD terminal V), so that every cross-regime gap V^l - V is identically zero at initialization and hence every jump-belief distortion g = exp(-(V^l - V)/xi) starts at exactly 1 for ALL xi, including the deepest. Controls FOC-consistent as above.
initialization_proposals.rationale: The analytic arm's post-mortem shows the killer is the minimizing player at initialization: level-right/shape-wrong differences amplified by 1/xi overflow before training starts. Starting belief-neutral makes the robust term vanish identically at step 0 regardless of xi — the distortions then grow only as training creates genuine cross-regime value gaps. This is the natural cold-start for the deep-xi wave, where cold and anchor currently have no chance, and it tests whether the degenerate no-investment collapse is caused by early jump-belief blowups rather than by the diffusion part of the problem.
